property_summary: Only the admin can change the owner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner, violating admin-only access control.

For any pair of calls to setOwner by different callers, the owner after the second call must equal the owner after the first call (because only admin can change it), but the mutant allows a non-admin to overwrite it.

For any two distinct callers where one is non-admin, the owner can never be set to the non-admin's address by that non-admin caller in the reference, but the mutant allows a non-admin to successfully set owner to any address.
The setOwner function must set the owner to the provided address parameter; the buggy version always sets it to msg.sender, violating this rule when the parameter differs from msg.sender.
After setOwner is called by the admin, the owner must equal the _owner argument passed, but the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead, so they differ when _owner != msg.sender.

Owner cannot be changed by a non-admin; the reference enforces this via the admin check, while the mutant allows the current owner to change ownership, violating the invariant that only the admin can update the owner.
For any caller, after any sequence of calls, if the admin is never setOwner, the owner must never change; the mutant allows the owner to change themselves without admin consent.

For any EOA call to setOwner, the call must revert if the caller is not the original admin; the mutant allows the current owner to call setOwner successfully, enabling ownership transfer without admin consent.
For any caller who is not the original admin (deployer), calling setOwner must revert; the mutant allows the current owner to call setOwner without revert, breaking the admin-only invariant.

For any caller and for any new owner address, the owner after calling setOwner(x) must remain unchanged if the caller is not the original deployer; the buggy mutant incorrectly allows the current owner (who may not be the deployer) to change the owner to a value different from the deployer's intent.

For any input, setOwner should either revert (if not admin) or succeed and return true after updating the owner; the buggy version returns false without changing the owner, so a call by the admin succeeds but returns false and leaves the owner unchanged.
